findings.title: select_value on a combobox now hard-fails when the AXValue write succeeds but the exact value isn't read back, instead of falling back to menu selection
findings.why_it_matters: Old code did `set_value_and_verify` then, on failure, fell through to `open_menu`/`wait_for_menu_item` (menu selection). New `select_combobox` only reaches `select_from_menu` when `set_ax_value_coerced` returns an Err with `not_delivered` disposition. When the write SUCCEEDS but `verify_value` can't observe the exact string (async UI update, value-vs-selection semantics, whitespace/formatting differences, or a combobox whose selection lives in AXSelectedChildren rather than AXValue), it returns Err and aborts the whole `select` command. A previously-working combobox select can now fail even though the value was set.
findings.suggested_fix: On successful AXValue write, if `verify_value` fails, fall through to `select_from_menu(element, value, deadline)` (the old behavior) rather than returning the error, OR only treat verify failure as a soft warning and return Ok(true)/Ok(false) instead of Err.

findings.title: ax_scroll aborts the entire scroll when try_value_shift reports 'write completed without movement', skipping sub-element arrows / page actions / physical fallbacks
findings.why_it_matters: `try_value_shift` returns `Err` (value_write_unverified) when the AXValue write reports success but the observed value didn't move in the expected direction. That `Err` is propagated by `?` at the call site, so `ax_scroll` returns immediately and never tries `try_sub_elements` (the increment/decrement arrow children), `perform_repeated_action(target, page_action, ...)`, or the physical keyboard/wheel fallbacks. A scrollbar that doesn't honor AXValue-set but has working arrow sub-elements or page actions will now fail to scroll where the old multi-mechanism chain would have succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a value-shift write that didn't move as a non-fatal 'mechanism unavailable' (return Ok(false)) so the caller continues to `try_sub_elements` / page actions / physical fallback, consistent with how `perform_repeated_action` returns Ok(false) for unsupported actions.

findings.title: list_apps now fails the entire inventory if any process in the ps snapshot lacks a process_instance token (e.g. exited between ps and lookup)
findings.why_it_matters: Old `list_apps()` was infallible and returned a best-effort `Vec<AppInfo>`, swallowing per-process errors. New `enrich_process_instances` calls `token_for_pid` per pid; `token_for_pid` returns `Ok(None)` when `ProcessIdentity::capture` finds no live instance (a process that exited in the gap between `ps` and the lookup, or one not resolvable). That `Ok(None)` hits `if app.process_instance.is_none() { return Err(...) }`, failing the WHOLE `list-apps` command. Cross-UID identity errors are correctly skipped via `continue`, but the `Ok(None)` case is not — an inconsistent and fragile policy that makes `list-apps` intermittently fail on busy systems with short-lived processes.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip (continue) instead of erroring when `resolve(pid)` yields `Ok(None)`, mirroring the cross-UID `continue` branch; only error on a genuine `Err`.

residual_risks: Notifications are fully stubbed to PlatformNotSupported (notifications/actions.rs, list.rs, nc_session.rs deleted; mod.rs test asserts all ops fail with PlatformNotSupported). AGENTS.md documents 4 working notification commands on macOS — this is a functional regression from the documented contract, likely an intentional rework, but callers/tests expecting working notification dismissal/action will break.
capture_app(pid) was removed and ScreenshotTarget no longer has an App variant; app-targeted screenshots are gone. Verify no core command or FFI path still expects an app screenshot path.

Role vocabulary changed: AXTabGroup->'tablist', AXRow->'row', AXScrollBar->'scrollbar', AXValueIndicator->'handle', AXSplitGroup->'group'. Any ref-allocation or capability logic keyed on the old normalized role strings (e.g. INTERACTIVE_ROLES membership, scroll-area ref targeting) may now mismatch. Scroll code uses native AX attribute strings so it is safe, but ref/role-dependent call sites should be re-checked.

Many new files are untracked (physical_click.rs, window_postcondition.rs, display.rs, scroll_read.rs, chain_value_write.rs, etc.) and are not visible in `git diff 52705af`. They are the least-reviewed code and must be compile-checked (cargo build) and integration-tested before merge.
testing_gaps: No test exercises the combobox select fallback path (AXValue write success + verify failure -> menu selection). The new behavior removes that fallback, so the regression in finding 1 is uncaught.
No test covers `try_value_shift` returning Err and the expectation that scroll continues to sub-elements/page/physical fallbacks; the new code aborts instead.

process_apps_tests.rs was heavily rewritten (111 lines changed) but appears to test the happy path; no test injects a process that exits mid-inventory (Ok(None) from token_for_pid) to confirm list_apps stays resilient.

The `every_notification_operation_fails_before_mutation` test in notifications/mod.rs asserts the NEW stubbed (PlatformNotSupported) behavior, effectively locking in the notification regression rather than guarding against it.
